58	- **État d'arrivée.** La partie noyau de l'état d'arrivée de `issue` (avec l'ancre ajoutée à `D(dst)` par le texte candidat) est l'état d'arrivée de `store`. C'est une égalité de structures (`issueEffR_eq`), pas une simple correspondance.
59	- **Clauses qui coïncident.**
60	  - `MetaRightM` est exactement l'exercice de `internal` en `Modify` exigé par O1.1 et O2.1 (`metaRightM_iff`).

98	  - Avec deux administrations, une région émise par l'autre donne `reject` au lieu de `fail` (`ce_two_admins`).

147	## (d) Statut des théorèmes de `DataStack`
148	
149	`DataStack` est une instance de bibliothèque. Son état contient l'état du noyau, les piles (stockage, `internal`, cellules ordonnées, sommet, blocs émis, marques vivantes) et le prochain identifiant de marque. Ses opérations n'effectuent que des pas du noyau :
150	
151	| Opération | Pas du noyau | Issues |
152	|---|---|---|
153	| `push` | clauses statiques de l'`issue` restreint (§77.1, §77.2) avant la place, puis `split` et `store` | `fail` sans place |
154	| `rewind` | `split` puis `release` (`reset` dérivé) sur les cellules au-dessus de la marque | `fail` pour une marque non vivante de la pile |
155	| `grow` | clauses statiques (dont `MetaRightM` et la destination hors de la nouvelle région) avant la place, puis `release` du dernier bloc et `issue` dérivé de même base et de taille plus grande vers la destination enregistrée (`Init`, ou `Moved` après un `transfer`) | `fail` sans place |
156	| `mark` | aucun (métadonnées) | `ok` sur une pile existante |
157	| `newStack` | aucun (inscription) | garde de §56 sur les deux registres |
158	
159	Un `newArena` du noyau consulte aussi le registre des piles (`KGuard`, §56). Tout pas `ok` de la bibliothèque est une suite de pas de `Reachable` (`dexec_reach`, `drun_reach`).
160	
161	| Théorème | Statut | Énoncé |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `rewind_rejects_live_above` | prouvé | marque vivante, autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvrant une cellule au-dessus de la marque ⟹ `rewind` = `reject` ; contraposée lue sur un `ok` : `rewind_ok_no_live_above` (la réciproque est fausse : `rewind` rejette aussi faute d'exercice de `internal`) |
164	| `mark_no_aba` | prouvé | **toute** marque retirée par `rewind m` (`m` et les marques postérieures de la pile) n'est plus vivante dans aucune pile après toute suite d'opérations, et son `rewind` échoue (`fail`), même quand le sommet revient à sa position. Hypothèse `MarksWF` (marques deux à deux distinctes, nommant leur pile, d'identifiants donnés), établie pour tout état atteint par la bibliothèque (`drun_init_marksWF`) |
165	| `rewind_removes` | prouvé | sous `MarksWF` : après `rewind m`, les marques de la pile sont exactement celles antérieures à `m` ; `m` et les postérieures sont retirées |
166	| `rewind_keeps_older_marks` | prouvé | après `rewind m` : marques = celles antérieures à `m`, sommet = sommet de `m`, autres piles inchangées, initialisation inchangée |
167	| `grow_same_base` | prouvé | dernier bloc de même base, de taille `size + extra`, de même destination enregistrée ; dans l'état d'arrivée, l'autorité nouvelle couvre les cellules depuis la même base et est détenue par cette destination, et l'ancien bloc est inactif ; anciennes cellules préfixe des nouvelles |
168	| `grow_keeps_prefix_init` | prouvé | aucune cellule de l'ancien bloc ne change d'initialisation |
169	| `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes` | prouvé, via `Ern.MM23` inchangé | voir ci-dessous |
170	
171	Détail de `grow_keeps_prefix_bytes`. `release` et `split` sont des pas sans pas MM-02 (`NoStep`, K4, dont `r6_noStep` conserve `Repr`). `store` correspond à une écriture de la plage de la destination (`storeOps`, L6). Pour toute disposition `LayoutWF`, cette écriture laisse inchangés les octets **et provenances** (`rangeBytes`) de chaque cellule de l'ancien bloc.
172	
173	Cas (`decide`, chaque exécution étant d'abord établie `ok`) :
174	
175	| Cas | Théorème | Contenu |
176	|---|---|---|
177	| plusieurs piles | `case_stacks` | piles indépendantes ; marque d'une autre pile : `fail` ; garde de §56 sur `newStack` et sur le `newArena` du noyau (que le noyau seul accepterait) |
178	| `rewind` refusé puis accepté | `case_rewind` | refusé tant que le bloc 7 vit, accepté après sa libération |
179	| ABA | `case_aba` | sommet revenu à 2 ; la marque retirée `⟨0, 1, 2⟩` échoue ; la nouvelle `⟨0, 2, 2⟩` est acceptée |
180	| `grow` | `case_grow` | accepté en place ; sans place : `fail` ; bloc qui n'est plus le dernier : `reject` |
181	| cadre | `case_frame` | marque à l'entrée de l'appelé, `push` dans un local ; `rewind` refusé tant que le bloc vit ; après `endUse` du local, `rewind` et `exitFrame` acceptés, pile vide |
182	| lecture de `rewind` | `case_rewind_reading` | une autorité dérivée active couvrant la partie d'une région émise après `m` qui est sous `m` (bloc agrandi) ou au-dessus du sommet courant ne bloque pas `rewind` ; un bloc vide (`push` de taille 0) non plus, et les métadonnées l'oublient alors qu'il reste actif |
183	| statique avant `fail` | `case_static_before_fail` | sans droit sur la valeur pile, `grow` est rejeté avec ou sans place ; `push` vers une destination `Init` est rejeté avec ou sans place ; `push` vers une destination intérieure aux cellules demandées, et `grow` vers une destination enregistrée intérieure à la nouvelle région, sont rejetés même sans place |
184	| atteignabilité | `cases_reachable` | les états noyau des cas sont atteints |

Il n'est alors exprimable qu'avec l'`issue` dérivé, `store` acceptant une cible `Init` ; `IssueR` le rejetterait (écart 2). Après un `transfer`, la destination enregistrée est `Moved`, et `IssueR` l'accepterait.

Sa relation exacte à `IssueR` n'est pas prouvée : `issue_as_kernel_split` porte sur une entrée du registre d'arènes, ce qu'une pile n'est pas, et la place y tient lieu de disponibilité.

Runs from `S3.init []` with the test contracts `K0` (no `SharedMutable` leaf) or `KA` (leaf 0
`SharedMutable`); every verdict by `decide`. -/

/-- Reachability of a run whose steps are all `ok`, under `K0`. -/
theorem reach_run {os : List Op} (h : (prun K0 (PS.init []) os).isSome = true) :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] os).s :=
  pReach_reachable (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (run_reach (by decide) h)

/-- Common prefix: frame 1 with the leaves 0 (arena value), 1 (storage), 2 and 3 (destinations), of
root authorities 0 to 3; `internal` 4 derived from 1 at `Modify` and stored into 0; `newArena 1 4`. -/
def opsArena : List Op :=
  [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .derive 1 1 .modify, .store 4 0, .newArena 1 4]

/-- The entry registered by `opsArena`. -/
def arD : Arena := ⟨1, 4, [1], []⟩

/-- **G2** (brief: "la clause G2 de `store` … n'introduit aucun rejet que `issue` n'a pas"): the
authority 5, derived from the root of the destination 2, is stored into the storage leaf 1, so that
2 is exercisable at `Modify` only through 5, hence through `internal` on 1. The restricted `issue` of
`[1]` into 2 is `ok`, and so is the kernel `issue`; in the arrival state the block on 1, held by 2,
and 5, held by 1, block each other, and 2 is no longer exercisable at `Modify`. `split` is `ok`, and
`store` of the block into 2 is rejected by its clause 5 (O8.5). An indirect cycle, which §88 allows
("des blocages indirects compatibles avec la sûreté peuvent subsister"). -/
def opsG2 : List Op := opsArena ++ [.derive 2 2 .modify, .store 5 1]

theorem ce_g2 :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsG2).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsG2).s.arenas = [arD] ∧
    IssueR arD [1] 2 (run K0 [] opsG2).s
      (.ok (issueEffR (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1] 2).1 (issueEffR (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1] 2).2) ∧
    IssueAt K0 0 0 [1] 2 (run K0 [] opsG2).s
      (.ok (arenaSet (issueEff (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1] 2).1 0
        (issueEff (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1] 2).2)) ∧
    ¬ HasRight (issueEffR (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1] 2).1 .modify 2 ∧
    SplitStep K0 4 [[1]] (run K0 [] opsG2).s
      (.ok ((run K0 [] opsG2).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1]))) ∧
    StoreStep (run K0 [] opsG2).s.A.length 2
      ((run K0 [] opsG2).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsG2).s arD [1])) .reject :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, .ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide),
    .ok (ar := arD) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)), by decide,
    .ok (by decide), .reject (by decide)⟩

/-- **Init** (sequence accepting more than `issue`): the destination 2 is written (`write3`) before
the emission. The restricted `issue` of `[1]` into 2 is rejected by clause 2 (§77.2, "non `Init`");
`split` then `store` of the block into 2 are `ok` (O8.2: "Le fait que ses données soient déjà `Init`
n'interdit pas à lui seul l'opération"). -/
def opsInit : List Op := opsArena ++ [.write 2 [2]]

theorem ce_init :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsInit).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsInit).s.arenas = [arD] ∧
    IssueR arD [1] 2 (run K0 [] opsInit).s .reject ∧
    SplitStep K0 4 [[1]] (run K0 [] opsInit).s
      (.ok ((run K0 [] opsInit).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsInit).s arD [1]))) ∧
    StoreStep (run K0 [] opsInit).s.A.length 2
      ((run K0 [] opsInit).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsInit).s arD [1]))
      (.ok (storeEff ((run K0 [] opsInit).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsInit).s arD [1]))
        (run K0 [] opsInit).s.A.length 2)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide), .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- The entry of `opsAvail` once `[1]` is issued (block 5) and the block released. -/
def arDu : Arena := ⟨1, 4, [], [([1], 5)]⟩

/-- **Availability** (the role of the metadata, §77.4): after the emission of `[1]` into 2 and the
release of the block, `internal` has its effective `Modify` on 1 again but the region is still
issued. The restricted `issue` of `[1]` into 3 fails; `split` then `store` into 3 are `ok`. -/
def opsAvail : List Op := opsArena ++ [.issue 0 0 [1] 2, .release 5]

theorem ce_avail :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsAvail).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsAvail).s.arenas = [arDu] ∧
    IssueR arDu [1] 3 (run K0 [] opsAvail).s (.fail (run K0 [] opsAvail).s arDu) ∧
    SplitStep K0 4 [[1]] (run K0 [] opsAvail).s
      (.ok ((run K0 [] opsAvail).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsAvail).s arDu [1]))) ∧
    StoreStep (run K0 [] opsAvail).s.A.length 3
      ((run K0 [] opsAvail).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsAvail).s arDu [1]))
      (.ok (storeEff ((run K0 [] opsAvail).s.addAuth (blockOf (run K0 [] opsAvail).s arDu [1]))
        (run K0 [] opsAvail).s.A.length 3)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, .fail (by decide) (by decide), .ok (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- **Empty region**: the restricted `issue` of the empty region is `ok` (the empty region is
available under the leaf reading of `available`, `ce_avail_leaf`); no place has an empty footprint
(`exists_mem_footprint`), so `derive` (O1), which takes a place, cannot produce the block, while
`split` on one region can (`issue_as_kernel_split`). -/
theorem ce_empty_region :
    IssueR arD [] 2 (run K0 [] opsArena).s
      (.ok (issueEffR (run K0 [] opsArena).s arD [] 2).1 (issueEffR (run K0 [] opsArena).s arD [] 2).2) ∧
    ∀ q < (run K0 [] opsArena).s.P.length, footprint (run K0 [] opsArena).s.P q ≠ [] := by
  refine ⟨.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide), fun q hq he => ?_⟩
  have hw := (reachable_invariants (KT_dd _ _ _ _ _) (reach_run (os := opsArena) (by decide))).1
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mem_footprint hw ((run K0 [] opsArena).s.P.length - q + 1) q (by omega) hq
  rw [he] at hl; simp at hl

/-- **`internal` stored into the arena value** (`reset`): `internal` 4 was placed into the arena
value 0 by `store` (O8), which adds it to `D 0`. The restricted `reset` and the kernel `reset` are
rejected by their clause 3 (§78.3, the kernel reading `internal` within its subtree of origins) for
as long as 0 is usable; `derive` of `internal` on the storage then `release` are `ok`. -/
theorem ce_reset_anchor :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsArena).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsArena).s.arenas = [arD] ∧
    4 ∈ (run K0 [] opsArena).s.D 0 ∧
    ¬ ResetPreR (run K0 [] opsArena).s arD ∧ ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (run K0 [] opsArena).s .reject ∧
    DeriveStep 4 1 .modify (run K0 [] opsArena).s
      (.ok (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsArena).s 4 1 .modify)) ∧
    ReleaseStep (run K0 [] opsArena).s.A.length (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsArena).s 4 1 .modify)
      (.ok (releaseEff (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsArena).s 4 1 .modify) (run K0 [] opsArena).s.A.length)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- An arena value that holds `internal` through `store` blocks the restricted `reset` while it is
usable. -/
theorem reset_blocked_by_stored_internal {s : S3} {ar : Arena} {v : Nat} (hv : s.Usable v)
    (hx : ar.internal ∈ s.D v) : ¬ ResetPreR s ar :=
  fun h => (h.2.2.2 v (List.mem_range.2 hv.lt) hv _ hx).1 rfl

/-- Prefix with an allocated storage: frame 1 with the leaves 0 (arena value), 1 (allocator
value), 2 and 3 (destinations); `alloc` of the storage 4, of parts 5 and 6, owned by 0, of root
authority 4 held by 0; `newArena 4 4`. `internal` is a root, in no `D`. -/
def opsAlloc : List Op :=
  [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1],
    .alloc 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)], .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4]

/-- The entry registered by `opsAlloc`. -/
def arL : Arena := ⟨4, 4, [5, 6], []⟩

/-- The entry of `opsAlloc` once `[5]` is issued into 2 (block 5). -/
def arLi : Arena := ⟨4, 4, [6], [([5], 5)]⟩

/-- **Leaf reading of `available`** (Q1I-1 of the review): after the emission of `[5]` (block 5,
active), the region `[5, 6]` partly overlaps the active emission. With `available` read leaf by leaf
(the kernel `Avail`), it is unavailable and the restricted `issue` fails (§77.4); with `available`
a set of regions from which only `[5]` left, `[5, 6]` would be available and §77.5 would reject it,
`internal` lacking the effective right on 5. The empty region is available though `available`
holds no region of it. -/
def opsLeaf : List Op := opsAlloc ++ [.issue 0 0 [5] 2]

theorem ce_avail_leaf :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsLeaf).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsLeaf).s.arenas = [arLi] ∧
    IssueR arLi [5, 6] 3 (run K0 [] opsLeaf).s (.fail (run K0 [] opsLeaf).s arLi) ∧
    ¬ IssueRight (run K0 [] opsLeaf).s arLi [5, 6] ∧ Avail arLi [] :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, .fail (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide⟩

/-- **Empty derivation** (`reset`): `split` of `internal` on the empty region creates an active
derivation of empty footprint. The restricted `reset` and the kernel `reset` are rejected by their
clause 2 (§78.2); `derive` of `internal` on the storage then `release` are `ok`. -/
def opsEmpty : List Op := opsAlloc ++ [.split 4 [[]]]

theorem ce_reset_empty :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s.arenas = [arL] ∧
    ¬ ResetPreR (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s arL ∧ ResetAtStep K0 0 0 (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s .reject ∧
    DeriveStep 4 4 .modify (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s
      (.ok (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s 4 4 .modify)) ∧
    ReleaseStep (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s.A.length (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s 4 4 .modify)
      (.ok (releaseEff (deriveEff (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s 4 4 .modify) (run K0 [] opsEmpty).s.A.length)) :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide, by decide, .reject (by decide), .ok (by decide),
    .ok (by decide)⟩

/-- Without such a derivation, the same arena is reset by both: the restricted `reset` holds. -/
theorem reset_alloc_ok : ResetPreR (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s arL := by decide

/-- The state `a6` of case 16 (`Ern.MM03`) is reached. -/
theorem a6_reachable : Reachable KA [] a6 := by
  have r0 : Reachable KA [] a0 := .enter (.init (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))
  have r1 : Reachable KA [] a1 := .write r0 (show Write3Step 1 [1] a0 (.ok a1) from .ok (by decide))
  have r2 : Reachable KA [] a2 := .alloc r1
    (show AllocStep KA 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0), (some 3, none, 0)] a1 (.ok a2) from
      .ok (by decide) trivial)
  have r3 : Reachable KA [] a3 := .newArena (.write r2 (show Write3Step 0 [0] a2 (.ok a2w) from
    .ok (by decide))) (show NewArenaStep 3 3 a2w (.ok a3) from .ok (by decide))
  have r4 : Reachable KA [] (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) :=
    .derive r3 (show DeriveStep 0 0 .observe a3 (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  have r5 : Reachable KA [] (deriveEff (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) 2 2 .modify) :=
    .derive r4 (show DeriveStep 2 2 .modify (deriveEff a3 0 0 .observe) (.ok _) from .ok (by decide))
  exact .enter r5 (show EnterStep [4, 5] [(none, none, 0)] _ (.ok a6) from .ok (by decide))

/-- **`writeShared` branch** (brief, question 1, counterexample to keep): in `a6`, case 16 of the
kernel, the callee frame has only the `Observe` authority 4 on the arena value 0, whose leaf is
`SharedMutable` under `KA`, and no block is issued. The kernel `issue` of `[4]` into 6 and the kernel
`reset` are `ok` through the `writeShared` branch of `MetaRight`; `internal` 3 is exercisable at no
`Modify` (`MetaRightM` fails), so `derive` of `internal` on the region (place 4) or on the storage
(place 3), and `split` on the region, are rejected; the restricted operations are rejected too. -/
theorem ce_writeShared :
    Reachable KA [] a6 ∧ a6.arenas = [ar7] ∧ ar7.issued = [] ∧
    IssueAt KA 0 4 [4] 6 a6 (.ok a7) ∧ ResetAtStep KA 0 4 a6 (.ok (resetAtEff a6 0)) ∧
    ¬ MetaRightM a6 ar7 ∧
    DeriveStep 3 4 .modify a6 .reject ∧ SplitStep KA 3 [[4]] a6 .reject ∧
    DeriveStep 3 3 .modify a6 .reject ∧
    IssueR ar7 [4] 6 a6 .reject ∧ ¬ ResetPreR a6 ar7 :=
  ⟨a6_reachable, by decide, rfl,
    .ok (ar := ar7) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)),
    .ok (by decide), by decide, .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide),
    .reject (by decide), by decide⟩

/-- **Two administrations** (`newArena_as_library`): the unguarded registration of `internal` 4 a
second time (`NewArenaPreNG` holds, the kernel guard rejects); the emission of `[5]` through entry 0
is `ok`; the emission of `[5]` through entry 1, whose metadata still has 5 available, is rejected by
the effective right (§77.5, §43 case 3), as is `split` of `internal` on `[5]`: the kernel rejects
the double emission, and the metadata of entry 1 no longer separates `fail` from `reject`. -/
def sTwo : S3 := newArenaEff (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4

def sTwoIssued : S3 := arenaSet (issueEff sTwo arL [5] 2).1 0 (issueEff sTwo arL [5] 2).2

theorem ce_two_admins :
    NewArenaPreNG (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4 ∧ NewArenaStep 4 4 (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s .reject ∧
    ReachableNG K0 [] sTwoIssued ∧ sTwoIssued.arenas.map (·.available) = [[6], [5, 6]] ∧
    IssueAt K0 1 0 [5] 3 sTwoIssued .reject ∧ IssueStatic K0 sTwoIssued arL 0 [5] 3 ∧
    Avail arL [5] ∧ SplitStep K0 4 [[5]] sTwoIssued .reject := by
  have h1 : NewArenaPreNG (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4 := by decide
  have hr : ReachableNG K0 [] sTwo :=
    .newArenaNG (reachableNG_of_reachable (reach_run (by decide))) h1
  refine ⟨h1, .reject (by decide), .step hr (.issue (via := 0) (.ok (ar := arL) (by decide)
    (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)))), by decide,
    .reject (ar := arL) (by decide) (.noRight (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)), by decide,
    by decide, .reject (by decide)⟩

/-- The state of `ce_two_admins` once the block 5, issued through entry 0, is released. -/
def sTwoReleased : S3 := releaseEff sTwoIssued 5

/-- **Two administrations, `fail` turned into `ok`** (follow-up review, R-1): after the release of
the block 5, entry 0 still lists `[5]` as issued and its emission of `[5]` fails (§77.4), while
entry 1, registered without the guard, issues `[5]` with `ok`. With the guard there is one entry,
and before a `reset` the region can only fail. No safety property is involved (the block is
inactive, `newArena_as_library`): what the guard keeps is the contract of the abstraction, an issued
region not issued again before `reset`. -/
theorem ce_two_admins_ok :
    ReachableNG K0 [] sTwoReleased ∧
    IssueAt K0 0 0 [5] 3 sTwoReleased (.fail sTwoReleased) ∧
    IssueAt K0 1 0 [5] 3 sTwoReleased
      (.ok (arenaSet (issueEff sTwoReleased arL [5] 3).1 1 (issueEff sTwoReleased arL [5] 3).2)) := by
  have h1 : NewArenaPreNG (run K0 [] opsAlloc).s 4 4 := by decide
  have hr : ReachableNG K0 [] sTwo :=
    .newArenaNG (reachableNG_of_reachable (reach_run (by decide))) h1
  have hr2 : ReachableNG K0 [] sTwoIssued := .step hr (.issue (via := 0) (.ok (ar := arL) (by decide)
    (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))))
  exact ⟨.step hr2 (.kernel (.release (.ok (by decide)))),
    .fail (ar := ⟨4, 4, [6], [([5], 5)]⟩) (by decide) (.fail (by decide) (by decide)),
    .ok (ar := arL) (by decide) (.ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide))⟩

/-- **Inexact metadata with the guard**: in a reached state, a frame that can exercise `internal`
derives from it directly (`derive` of 4 on 5 at `Observe`); the region `[5]` is available in the
metadata and its emission is rejected by the effective right. The guard does not make the metadata
exact either. -/
def opsObs : List Op := opsAlloc ++ [.derive 4 5 .observe]

theorem ce_avail_reject :
    Reachable K0 [] (run K0 [] opsObs).s ∧ (run K0 [] opsObs).s.arenas = [arL] ∧
    IssueAt K0 0 0 [5] 2 (run K0 [] opsObs).s .reject ∧ IssueStatic K0 (run K0 [] opsObs).s arL 0 [5] 2 ∧
    Avail arL [5] :=
  ⟨reach_run (by decide), by decide,
    .reject (ar := arL) (by decide) (.noRight (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)), by decide, by decide⟩

end Ern.Derived.Arena

9:## État de vérification
23:## Résultats principaux
48:## (a) Clause → déclaration
73:## (b) Statut
138:## (c) Décisions
252:## (d) Non prouvé
280:## (e) Questions
325:## (f) Hypothèses de `simulation`
354:## Revue adverse

## (e) Questions

1. **L7 et les feuilles de taille nulle.** K1 (d) permet une plage vide. Une feuille de plage vide
   est disjointe en octets d'elle-même ; l'instanciation de L7 déclare alors une région disjointe
   d'elle-même, et `DDSound` échoue (`ddSound_of_layout_needs_size`, avec un témoin `LayoutWF`). Le
   module ajoute l'hypothèse « plages non vides » aux feuilles des régions déclarées. Pour un
   programme qui déclare disjointe une région contenant une feuille de taille nulle, L7 ne décharge
   donc pas l'hypothèse `DDSound k` de `simulation`. Faut-il garder cette hypothèse, exclure les
   feuilles de taille nulle des déclarations, ou lire `DDSound` sans les feuilles de taille nulle ?
2. **Pointeur d'une région vide.** L6 définit l'adresse du pointeur par sa première feuille, qui
   n'existe pas pour une région vide. Le brouillon accepte les deux cas suivants.
   - `issue` d'un bloc vide (`[]`) est `ok`. Le module écrit l'adresse 0 et la provenance du
     stockage de l'arène, que L6 fixe. Témoin `CaseSim` : `issue` de `[]` vers la feuille 7.
   - `split` en une sous-région vide est `ok` (MM-03.3 O2 permet des sous-régions de taille
     nulle), puis `store` de l'autorité obtenue. Le module écrit l'adresse 0, sans provenance.
     Témoin `CaseSim.x10e` : `split 6 [[]]` puis `store 10 8`.

   Quelle adresse, et pour `store` quelle provenance, faut-il au pointeur d'une région vide ? Ou
   faut-il rejeter ces opérations ?
3. **Première feuille ou premier octet.** L6 demande que `decode` rende « l'adresse du premier octet
   de la région (base + off de la première feuille) ». Le module lit « première feuille » comme la
   tête de la liste qui représente la région. Les deux lectures divergent dès que la tête n'a pas le
   plus petit décalage. Témoins `CaseSim` :
   - `issue` de `[6, 5]`, `ok` : pointeur 112, adresse de 6, alors que la région commence en 104 ;
   - avec la disposition `Lsw`, qui échange les deux champs (K1 ne fixe pas leur ordre) et
     satisfait `LayoutWF`, la région `[5, 6]` donne 112 alors qu'elle commence en 104.

   Faut-il l'adresse la plus basse des feuilles de la région ? Et que faire d'une feuille de taille
   nulle placée avant les autres ?
4. **Taille de la cible d'un pointeur.** `PtrEncAt` porte sur la suite des octets du pointeur ; la
   plage de la cible n'en reçoit que `(L p).len`. Rien n'exige que cette taille suffise à
   `decode`, et K1 (d) permet une taille nulle. Témoin `CaseSim.L0` : `ReprB` tient, le pointeur
   écrit par `store 5 8` se décode toujours en 8, mais la plage de 8 ne reçoit aucun octet, alors
   que MM-03 rend 8 `Init` et lui fait détenir l'autorité 5. Faut-il une hypothèse (spec 4 ou 11) :
   la feuille qui reçoit une référence a la taille d'un pointeur, et `decode` ne lit que ces
   octets ?
5. **`SameSizeAlong` et les types (spec 4).** `transfer` du brouillon compare les formes
   (`SameShape`), pas les tailles ni le champ `kind` des places. L6 pose `SameSizeAlong` en
   hypothèse. Faut-il que `SameShape` compare aussi les `kind`, pour qu'une disposition fonction du
   type donne `SameSizeAlong` ?
6. **Forme de `simulation`.** Les obligations portent sur l'exécution donnée et sur les paramètres
   fixés (`SimRun`, (c) 14), pas sur une exécution `Reachable` quelconque ; (d) 1 dit pourquoi elles
   ne se déchargent pas en général. Cette lecture de « les hypothèses restantes sont listées dans
   l'énoncé » est-elle la bonne ?

## (f) Hypothèses de `simulation`

Les hypothèses de `simulation` sont de trois sortes : celles de l'énoncé, globales ; les prémisses
de `SimRun`, qui portent sur l'exécution et sa traduction avec les paramètres `π` fixés une fois ;
l'enveloppe de `Step3`, fixée par L1 et L2. Chacune est classée ci-dessous : spec 4 (types),
spec 11 (ABI), bibliothèque, ouverte.

theorem dealloc_invalidates {Compatible : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel Compatible]
    {ObR : ReadObl} {ObW : WriteObl} {ac : Access} {auth : Nat}
    {s s' : State} (h : dealloc Compatible ac.prov auth s = .ok s') :
    (∀ hs, read ObR ac s' hs = .ub) ∧ ∀ w hs, write ObW ac w s' hs = .ub := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := dealloc_eq_ok.1 h
  obtain ⟨hr, hw⟩ := dealloc_invalidates_pre s ac
  exact ⟨fun _ => by simp [read, hr], fun _ _ => by simp [write, hw]⟩

/-- P2c, MM-02.D et MM-02.H : après une désallocation brute réussie de `id`, une
nouvelle désallocation brute de `id`, avec toute autorité, a pour issue `ub`. -/
theorem no_double_free {Compatible : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel Compatible]
    {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State}
    (h : dealloc Compatible id auth s = .ok s') (auth' : Nat) :
    dealloc Compatible id auth' s' = .ub := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := dealloc_eq_ok.1 h
  simp [dealloc, no_double_free_pre Compatible s id auth']

/-- P2b, MM-02.A et MM-02.H : après la désallocation brute réussie de
l'allocation visée par `ac`, puis une allocation brute réussie de base `base`
quelconque (y compris la base de l'ancienne), toute lecture et toute écriture
brutes par `ac` ont pour issue `ub`. -/
theorem reuse_does_not_restore {Compatible : Nat → Nat → Prop} [DecidableRel Compatible]
    {ObR : ReadObl} {ObW : WriteObl}
    {ac : Access} {auth : Nat} (space base size align : Nat) (freeAuth : Option Nat)
    {s s₁ s₂ : State} (h₁ : dealloc Compatible ac.prov auth s = .ok s₁) {hwf₁ : WF s₁}
    (h₂ : alloc space base size align freeAuth s₁ hwf₁ = .ok s₂) :
    (∀ hs, read ObR ac s₂ hs = .ub) ∧ ∀ w hs, write ObW ac w s₂ hs = .ub := by
  obtain ⟨⟨a, ha, -⟩, hs₁⟩ := dealloc_eq_ok.1 h₁
  obtain ⟨⟨hf, -⟩, hs₂⟩ := alloc_eq_ok.1 h₂
  have hd : s₁.allocs ac.prov = some { a with live := false } := by
    subst hs₁
    simp [State.dealloc, ha]
  have hne : ac.prov ≠ s₁.next := fun e => by
    rw [e, hf] at hd
    cases hd
  · rfl

/-- MM-02.C et MM-02.B : relire la plage qu'une écriture valide par `ac` vient
d'écrire, par un accès de même provenance, adresse et longueur et d'autorité `r`
quelconque, rend le contenu écrit. -/
theorem readBytes_write_same {s : State} {ac : Access} (hw : CanWrite s ac)
    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (r : Auth) :
    readBytes (s.write ac w) { ac with auth := r } =
      some ((List.range ac.len).map fun i => .init (w i).1 (w i).2) := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, hl, hsp, -⟩ := hw
  have hwa : (s.write ac w).allocs ac.prov = some (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) := by
    simp [State.write, ha]
  have hR : Read (s.write ac w) { ac with auth := r } :=
    ⟨_, hwa, hl, hsp, fun i hi => by
      show (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).bytes (ac.addr - a.base + i) ≠ .uninit
      rw [Alloc.write_bytes_in a w hi]
      nofun, Or.inl rfl⟩
  show (match (s.write ac w).allocs ac.prov with
    | some a => if Read (s.write ac w) { ac with auth := r } then
        some (a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len) else none
    | none => none) = _
  rw [hwa]
  dsimp only
  rw [ite_eq_left hR]
  congr 1
  exact List.map_congr_left fun i hi => Alloc.write_bytes_in a w (List.mem_range.1 hi)

/-- MM-02.C et MM-02.B : une écriture valide par `ac` ne change pas la lecture par
`ac'` si `ac'` a une autre provenance, ou si les plages d'adresses des deux accès
sont disjointes. -/
theorem readBytes_write_other {s : State} {ac ac' : Access} (hw : CanWrite s ac)
    (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
    (hd : ac'.prov ≠ ac.prov ∨ RangeDisjoint ac.addr ac.len ac'.addr ac'.len) :
    readBytes (s.write ac w) ac' = readBytes s ac' := by
  by_cases hp : ac'.prov = ac.prov
  case neg => exact readBytes_congr (by simp [State.write, hp])
theorem read_sound_ok {ObR : ReadObl} {ac : Access} {s s' : State} {hs : ObR.stat s ac}
    (h : read ObR ac s hs = .ok s') :
    s' = s ∧ ∃ v, readBytes s ac = some v ∧ ReadStep ObR.toSpec ac s (.ok v) := by
  obtain ⟨⟨hR, hd⟩, rfl⟩ := read_eq_ok.1 h
  have ⟨a, ha, _⟩ := hR
  exact ⟨rfl, _, readBytes_eq_some_iff.2 ⟨hR, a, ha, rfl⟩, .ok ha ⟨hR, hd, hs⟩⟩

/-- MM-02.B et MM-02.H : si l'interpréteur `read`, appelé avec une preuve de la
part statique, rend `ub`, alors `ub` est l'issue de la sémantique `ReadStep`. -/
theorem read_sound_ub {ObR : ReadObl} {ac : Access} {s : State} {hs : ObR.stat s ac}
    (h : read ObR ac s hs = .ub) : ReadStep ObR.toSpec ac s .ub :=
  .ub fun ⟨h1, h2, _⟩ => read_eq_ub.1 h ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- MM-02.B et MM-02.H : si la sémantique `ReadStep` a l'issue `ok v`, alors pour
toute preuve de la part statique l'interpréteur `read` rend `ok s` et `readBytes`
rend `v`. -/
theorem read_complete_ok {ObR : ReadObl} {ac : Access} {s : State} {v : List AByte}
    (h : ReadStep ObR.toSpec ac s (.ok v)) :
    ∀ hs, read ObR ac s hs = .ok s ∧ readBytes s ac = some v := by
  intro hs

def IssueStaticR (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  MetaRightM s ar ∧ s.Active ar.internal ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ s.afp ar.internal) ∧
  s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧
  isLeaf s.P dst ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst)
    True) ∧
  dst ∉ region

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueStaticR s ar region dst) := by
  unfold IssueStaticR; infer_instance

/-- The static preconditions of the restricted `issue` are those of the kernel `issue`
(`IssueStatic`) with the restricted right and the destination outside the region. -/
theorem issueStaticR_iff {k : K} {via : Nat} {s : S3} {ar : Arena} {region : List Nat}
    {dst : Nat} : IssueStaticR s ar region dst ↔
      MetaRightM s ar ∧ IssueStatic k s ar via region dst ∧ dst ∉ region := by
  unfold IssueStaticR IssueStatic
  exact ⟨fun ⟨h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8⟩ => ⟨h0, ⟨.inl h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7⟩, h8⟩,
    fun ⟨h0, ⟨_, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7⟩, h8⟩ => ⟨h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8⟩⟩

/-- Effect of the restricted `issue` (candidate Spec 1 §77, effect): the effect of the kernel
(`issueEff`: the block, held by the destination, which alone becomes `Init`; the region leaves
`available` and joins `issued`), and the destination "reçoit l'ancre correspondante": the block is
added to `D dst`, which the kernel `issueEff` does not do. -/
def issueEffR (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 × Arena :=
  ({ (issueEff s ar region dst).1 with
      D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ [s.A.length] else s.D q },
   (issueEff s ar region dst).2)

/-- Checks of the restricted `issue` on the simulated arrival state (candidate Spec 1 §77.3 and
§77.6): `AnchorOrder` for the new anchor of the destination, and `AnchorOrderHeld`. -/
def ArrivalR (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  EffAnchorOK (issueEffR s ar region dst).1 s.A.length ((issueEffR s ar region dst).1.pframe dst) ∧
  AnchorOrderHeld (issueEffR s ar region dst).1

instance (s : S3) (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (ArrivalR s ar region dst) := by
  unfold ArrivalR; infer_instance

/-- The restricted `issue` as a relation (candidate Spec 1 §77; §58): `reject` when a static
precondition fails; `fail`, the state unchanged, when the region is not available (§77.4);
`reject` when `internal` lacks effective `Modify` on the region (§77.5) or an arrival check fails
(§77.3, §77.6); `ok` otherwise. The disjointness of §77.5 from the active emissions is not
restated: it follows from the effective right (`issue_disjoint_redundant`, A11).

Availability is the kernel `Avail`, read leaf by leaf: the kernel keeps `available` as a list of
leaves, where §46 types it `Set<Region>` and §77.4 tests whether the region belongs to it. The text
does not settle which reading holds, and the readings classify differently: under the leaf reading a
region that partly overlaps an active emission fails (§77.4) instead of reaching §77.5, and the
empty region is always available (`ce_avail_leaf`; report, (f)). -/
inductive IssueR (ar : Arena) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (s : S3) : IOutcome → Prop where
  | ok : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → Avail ar region → IssueRight s ar region →
      ArrivalR s ar region dst →
      IssueR ar region dst s (.ok (issueEffR s ar region dst).1 (issueEffR s ar region dst).2)
  | fail : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → ¬ Avail ar region → IssueR ar region dst s (.fail s ar)
  | reject : ¬ IssueStaticR s ar region dst → IssueR ar region dst s .reject
  | noRight : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → Avail ar region → ¬ IssueRight s ar region →
      IssueR ar region dst s .reject
  | noAnchor : IssueStaticR s ar region dst → Avail ar region → IssueRight s ar region →
      ¬ ArrivalR s ar region dst → IssueR ar region dst s .reject

/-- Determinism of the restricted `issue`. -/

## 0. How the material defines "class" and "twin" (and the other corpus rules)

Mat. §0 (rules of jalon 3), quoted in substance:

- **Rule 1, oracle.** "Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer »." For the reference, the sources MM-02 v0.4 / MM-03.3 v0.3 are superseded by spec v0; expected verdicts must be re-derived from spec v0 clauses (column "spec v0" below), and every change against the material verdict is reported, not applied silently (rule 4).
- **Rule 2, twin.** "**Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction." For MM2-H the table has an explicit column "Jumeau `ok`" (twin of a `ub`). The material itself pairs H37 (ok) with H21b (reject) as "jumeau négatif".
- **Rule 3, reached states.** "Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés."
- **Rule 4.** "Pas de correction silencieuse. Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause."
- **Rule 5, class.** "**Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3." MM2-H and MM23-H tables have no class column (MM2-H is N2 by construction; MM23-H is R; J3 assigned H14 → spec 3, H17 → spec 4/11). W1–W3 are not classed by the material (J3 (f) 17 chose Lib).
- **Rule 6, coverage** ("Couvert": earlier witness). **Rule 7**: MM2-H "validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence". **Rule 8, known gaps**: a case resting on an unapplied decision (MM23-H15, H16) is "encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu » … jamais présenté comme réussi". The brief now requires H15/H16 to pass.

Draft pattern satisfying rules 2–3 (reusable, see §5): `run` from `PS.init statics` with a frame-less fallback `stuckPS` (H3:27, H3:37), `run_reach` (H3:48), `run_ok_of_reach` (H3:54); `sst`/`sstuck`, `sim_of`, `sst_ok_of_reachable` (H23:264, H23:273, H23:301, H23:353); `drun`/`final`/`final_reach` (DS:268, DS:887, DS:890). ## 4. Spec problems (with passage and example)

**P1. `HandlePool` and `DataStack` contracts are outside `specs/`, yet the brief requires their verdicts.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Spec v0 constrains them only through §36 (`MetaRight`), §56 (guard), §37 and §89 ("a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure"), §9. Examples with no deciding clause: H31b (`resolveMany Modify` with two handles on one entry → `fail` or `reject`?); `pool_free_entry_handle` H3:977 (`freeSlot` of a free slot at its current generation: v0.4 D.3 only says it "n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité"); `case_aba` DS:927 (`rewind` of a removed mark → `fail`); `freeSlot` with a derived `internal` (v0.4 D.3 vs §69.2 literal). These verdicts cannot be fixed from the spec.

**P2. MM23-H15/H16 expected verdicts rest on jalon-2 decisions 2 and 3, which spec v0 does not contain.** §82.3: "an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into a single logical leaf with an appropriate representation"; §81 leaves "representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); … encodings (Spec 11)" undetermined. Example: run R6 (H23:745) `issue [5, 4]` into 2, leaf 4 at offset 0, leaf 5 at offset 8: writing address base+8 (head) or base (lowest) both satisfy §82 as written. The brief says H15/H16 "must now pass"; that requires a recorded decision (spec text or DESIGN.md parameter of the refinement relation), not a silent choice.

**P3. MM23-H09: deallocation of automatic storage at `exitFrame` is not specified.** §9: "The kernel also represents storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later." §73: "Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places." Example: R1 exit (H23:503) — a realization emitting three `DeallocStep` for locals 0, 1, 2 and one emitting none both satisfy §73 and §82.5; the material expects three.

**P4. Byte-copy provenance (MM2-H13a, MM23-H04/H13).** §10: "Rules for propagation of provenance during byte copies and reinterpretations are not yet fixed"; §19: "Undecided: … propagation through representation copies." Against §20.2 (a read "supplies the sequence of abstract bytes actually read, including provenance") and §16 (a write stores "the supplied representation and its provenance information"). Example: `ReadStep` of an 8-byte pointer returns `[init v (some a)]×8`; a `WriteStep` supplying those abstract bytes stores `some a` by §16, but §10 says the copy's propagation is not fixed. H13a "la provenance de chaque octet est conservée" holds at relation level only if the copy supplies the read abstract bytes; at language level it is open.

**P5. `transfer` creating an ownership cycle not caught by any listed precondition.** §63 lists no arrival-usability clause; §63.8 checks only `corr(r)`; §58: "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants." Example: x (Init) owns y (alloc owner x), y owns z (alloc owner y, leaf, Uninit); `transfer(x, z)`: §63.1–§63.5 hold; §63.6–§63.7 are vacuous for the then-unusable places; §63.8 holds (root of y covers leaves of y, `corr(x) = z` ∉ footprint(y)); effect: y owned by z, z owned by y — an ownership cycle (§40 "An ownership cycle makes no place usable"), active roots of y and z covering unusable places (`NoDangling`, §54). Whether §58 acts as an implicit rejection is not stated. The draft has an explicit clause "`(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst`" (M3:1243) which spec v0 does not list. Concerns H13's class of cases.

**P6. Frame ownership of `enterFrame` locals is implicit.** §72.2: "introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots"; §39: "Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places"; §70.1 speaks of "an ordinary local directly owned by a frame"; §47 explicitly allows a static owned by another static, with no analogue for locals. Example: H27b's draft shape `(none, some 0, 0)` (H3:505), a local root owned by local 0, is not excluded by any §72 clause; it would be an `OwnedRoot` freeable by §70. The brief treats "locals owned by frame" as a spec v0 rule; the text does not state it.

**P7 (outside corpus scope, for the kernel mapper).** §36: "Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations" vs §71.2: provider "updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, frame holding only `Observe` on it, `alloc(provider, owner, shape)` passes §71's static preconditions. No corpus case uses it.

**Corpus verdicts superseded by spec v0 (rule 1 source change, to be reported, not silent):** H21 ok → reject (§36, §77.1); H50 à arbitrer → reject (§63.8, §77.2); H49, H51 à arbitrer → ok with residual blocking (§65 last ¶, §88); pool witnesses of 1.5.

## 5. Representation choices recommended (change no accepted program)

1. One library-state record beside `S₃` holding all administration registries (arenas, pools, stacks), with one "live `internal` identities" view used by every creation op — §56 requires consulting all registries; how they are stored is free (§56 "Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel").
2. Drop the `via` argument of library ops once `MetaRight` is Modify-only (it no longer selects anything).
3. Keep the draft case pattern: executable run from the initial state, proven sound, with a fallback state that no run reaches (`stuckPS` H3:27, `sstuck` H23:264), verdict stated with the relation, twin in the same theorem.
4. Arena ops as functions on (kernel state, library state) with a theorem "library `ok` ⇒ kernel step sequence" (draft `issue_as_kernel_split` DA:611, `reset_as_kernel` DA:826, `dexec_reach` DS:412 are the models).
5. Uniform `fail` representation for library ops (state unchanged): either `fail` without state (DS:68) or `fail s` with `s` the input (HP:73), not both.
6. One corpus module per corpus (MM2-H, MM3-H + W, MM23-H, new cases), cases named by material ID, docstring = material summary + spec v0 clauses + class + "material verdict / spec v0 verdict" when they differ.
7. Record unencoded cases (section J, H13b, MM23-H14/H17) as docstring-only entries with their destination, no theorem.

## 0. How the material defines "class" and "twin" (and the other corpus rules)

Mat. §0 (rules of jalon 3), quoted in substance:

- **Rule 1, oracle.** "Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer »." For the reference, the sources MM-02 v0.4 / MM-03.3 v0.3 are superseded by spec v0; expected verdicts must be re-derived from spec v0 clauses (column "spec v0" below), and every change against the material verdict is reported, not applied silently (rule 4).
- **Rule 2, twin.** "**Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction." For MM2-H the table has an explicit column "Jumeau `ok`" (twin of a `ub`). The material itself pairs H37 (ok) with H21b (reject) as "jumeau négatif".
- **Rule 3, reached states.** "Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés."
- **Rule 4.** "Pas de correction silencieuse. Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause."
- **Rule 5, class.** "**Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3." MM2-H and MM23-H tables have no class column (MM2-H is N2 by construction; MM23-H is R; J3 assigned H14 → spec 3, H17 → spec 4/11). W1–W3 are not classed by the material (J3 (f) 17 chose Lib).
- **Rule 6, coverage** ("Couvert": earlier witness). **Rule 7**: MM2-H "validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence". **Rule 8, known gaps**: a case resting on an unapplied decision (MM23-H15, H16) is "encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu » … jamais présenté comme réussi". The brief now requires H15/H16 to pass.

Draft pattern satisfying rules 2–3 (reusable, see §5): `run` from `PS.init statics` with a frame-less fallback `stuckPS` (H3:27, H3:37), `run_reach` (H3:48), `run_ok_of_reach` (H3:54); `sst`/`sstuck`, `sim_of`, `sst_ok_of_reachable` (H23:264, H23:273, H23:301, H23:353); `drun`/`final`/`final_reach` (DS:268, DS:887, DS:890). Verdicts are stated with the operation's relation (`TransferStep … .reject`, etc.) on the reached state.

## 4. Spec problems (with passage and example)

**P1. `HandlePool` and `DataStack` contracts are outside `specs/`, yet the brief requires their verdicts.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Spec v0 constrains them only through §36 (`MetaRight`), §56 (guard), §37 and §89 ("a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure"), §9. Examples with no deciding clause: H31b (`resolveMany Modify` with two handles on one entry → `fail` or `reject`?); `pool_free_entry_handle` H3:977 (`freeSlot` of a free slot at its current generation: v0.4 D.3 only says it "n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité"); `case_aba` DS:927 (`rewind` of a removed mark → `fail`); `freeSlot` with a derived `internal` (v0.4 D.3 vs §69.2 literal). These verdicts cannot be fixed from the spec.

**P2. MM23-H15/H16 expected verdicts rest on jalon-2 decisions 2 and 3, which spec v0 does not contain.** §82.3: "an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into a single logical leaf with an appropriate representation"; §81 leaves "representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); … encodings (Spec 11)" undetermined. Example: run R6 (H23:745) `issue [5, 4]` into 2, leaf 4 at offset 0, leaf 5 at offset 8: writing address base+8 (head) or base (lowest) both satisfy §82 as written. The brief says H15/H16 "must now pass"; that requires a recorded decision (spec text or DESIGN.md parameter of the refinement relation), not a silent choice.

**P3. MM23-H09: deallocation of automatic storage at `exitFrame` is not specified.** §9: "The kernel also represents storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later." §73: "Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places." Example: R1 exit (H23:503) — a realization emitting three `DeallocStep` for locals 0, 1, 2 and one emitting none both satisfy §73 and §82.5; the material expects three.

**P4. Byte-copy provenance (MM2-H13a, MM23-H04/H13).** §10: "Rules for propagation of provenance during byte copies and reinterpretations are not yet fixed"; §19: "Undecided: … propagation through representation copies." Against §20.2 (a read "supplies the sequence of abstract bytes actually read, including provenance") and §16 (a write stores "the supplied representation and its provenance information"). Example: `ReadStep` of an 8-byte pointer returns `[init v (some a)]×8`; a `WriteStep` supplying those abstract bytes stores `some a` by §16, but §10 says the copy's propagation is not fixed. H13a "la provenance de chaque octet est conservée" holds at relation level only if the copy supplies the read abstract bytes; at language level it is open.

**P5. `transfer` creating an ownership cycle not caught by any listed precondition.** §63 lists no arrival-usability clause; §63.8 checks only `corr(r)`; §58: "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants." Example: x (Init) owns y (alloc owner x), y owns z (alloc owner y, leaf, Uninit); `transfer(x, z)`: §63.1–§63.5 hold; §63.6–§63.7 are vacuous for the then-unusable places; §63.8 holds (root of y covers leaves of y, `corr(x) = z` ∉ footprint(y)); effect: y owned by z, z owned by y — an ownership cycle (§40 "An ownership cycle makes no place usable"), active roots of y and z covering unusable places (`NoDangling`, §54). Whether §58 acts as an implicit rejection is not stated. The draft has an explicit clause "`(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst`" (M3:1243) which spec v0 does not list. Concerns H13's class of cases.

**P6. Frame ownership of `enterFrame` locals is implicit.** §72.2: "introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots"; §39: "Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places"; §70.1 speaks of "an ordinary local directly owned by a frame"; §47 explicitly allows a static owned by another static, with no analogue for locals. Example: H27b's draft shape `(none, some 0, 0)` (H3:505), a local root owned by local 0, is not excluded by any §72 clause; it would be an `OwnedRoot` freeable by §70. The brief treats "locals owned by frame" as a spec v0 rule; the text does not state it.

**P7 (outside corpus scope, for the kernel mapper).** §36: "Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations" vs §71.2: provider "updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, frame holding only `Observe` on it, `alloc(provider, owner, shape)` passes §71's static preconditions. No corpus case uses it.

**Material ambiguities (not spec defects; keep both readings, rule 4):** H01 reborrow reading (J3 (g) 5; spec v0 §45/§72 accept it); W2 "la vue de colonne" (J3 (g) 6); W3 blocks issued to locals or into the structure (J3 (g) 7); H16 by-value reception (no kernel primitive; §45 defers to Spec 3); W1–W3 class not given.

**Corpus verdicts superseded by spec v0 (rule 1 source change, to be reported, not silent):** H21 ok → reject (§36, §77.1); H50 à arbitrer → reject (§63.8, §77.2); H49, H51 à arbitrer → ok with residual blocking (§65 last ¶, §88); pool witnesses of 1.5.

## 5. Representation choices recommended (change no accepted program)

1. One library-state record beside `S₃` holding all administration registries (arenas, pools, stacks), with one "live `internal` identities" view used by every creation op — §56 requires consulting all registries; how they are stored is free (§56 "Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel").
2. Drop the `via` argument of library ops once `MetaRight` is Modify-only (it no longer selects anything).
3. Keep the draft case pattern: executable run from the initial state, proven sound, with a fallback state that no run reaches (`stuckPS` H3:27, `sstuck` H23:264), verdict stated with the relation, twin in the same theorem.
4. Arena ops as functions on (kernel state, library state) with a theorem "library `ok` ⇒ kernel step sequence" (draft `issue_as_kernel_split` DA:611, `reset_as_kernel` DA:826, `dexec_reach` DS:412 are the models).
5. Uniform `fail` representation for library ops (state unchanged): either `fail` without state (DS:68) or `fail s` with `s` the input (HP:73), not both.
6. One corpus module per corpus (MM2-H, MM3-H + W, MM23-H, new cases), cases named by material ID, docstring = material summary + spec v0 clauses + class + "material verdict / spec v0 verdict" when they differ.
7. Record unencoded cases (section J, H13b, MM23-H14/H17) as docstring-only entries with their destination, no theorem.

Not checked: Lean was not built or run (verdicts "obtained" are those stated by the draft theorems and J3/DER); spec v0 verdicts for H11, H44, W3 under the new `D(dst)` anchor were traced by hand, not executed.
